title: Living ashtpadi 3
hook: the Name first, and deeds to match it

segments.voice: Yesterday, the best of all ways, and your line: name and pure deeds. Did you do your clean deed and keep it to yourself? Today, living the third ashtpadi. Day four hundred forty-nine.

Everyone knows the gap. The friend who says, let's get coffee soon, and never does. The company whose website is full of the word integrity. The version of yourself that, on Sunday night, says this week will be different. Words are easy. They cost nothing until you have to live inside them. And most of us have been let down, at least once, by someone whose words and deeds didn't match. The third ashtpadi of Sukhmani is, in the end, about closing that gap.
screen: `LET'S GET COFFEE SOON.` → `INTEGRITY ON THE WEBSITE.` → `THE GAP BETWEEN WORD AND DEED.`

segments.voice: Gather the third ashtpadi. Its salok: I have searched many scriptures, and nothing equals the Name. Its long list: chanting, fasting, ritual, pilgrimage, forest, fire, none of them equal reflecting on the Name, because washing the body doesn't wash the mind. And its final ladder: the highest way is to chant the Name and do pure deeds. Put those side by side and a shape appears. The ashtpadi is suspicious of outside without inside, of the ritual done while pride sits untouched. But it's just as clear that the inside has to come out. The Name comes first, and then deeds to match it. Nirmal karam, clean action, sits right beside remembering at the top of the ladder. Guru Nanak said the same thing in one of the best-known lines in the Guru Granth Sahib, in Sri Raag. In paraphrase: truth is higher than everything, but higher still is truthful living. Many Sikhs know that line by heart. Not truth as an idea you agree with. Truth as a way you live. That's what living the third ashtpadi looks like on an ordinary day. The Name on your lips in the morning, and then the same Name visible in how you treat the cashier, the coworker, the person in the next car. Say it, then do it. Sikh life builds this into its shape: Naam japna, remembering the Name, sits next to kirat karni, honest work, and vand chhakna, sharing what you have. Remembering, earning, sharing: words and deeds, together.
screen: `THE SALOK, THE LIST, THE LADDER.` · `OUTSIDE WITHOUT INSIDE FAILS.` · `HIGHER STILL: TRUTHFUL LIVING.` · `REMEMBER, WORK HONESTLY, SHARE.` · then, large: `SAY IT, DO IT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: match one word to a deed. Think of something you've said recently and haven't done yet. I'll call you. I'll help with that. I'll be more patient. Pick one. Hold it in mind for a breath, without guilt, just looking at it. Then decide one small step that would make the word true, today if possible. Picture yourself taking that step. If you pray, say Waheguru once, and let the word and the deed meet. The bell holds the time.
Living ashtpadi 3. Sukhmani's third section in daily life: the Name first, and deeds to match it, because truthful living is higher still.
Your line: say it, do it. Today, take the one small step that makes your word true, before the day ends. Day four hundred forty-nine.

howItsDone: Sikhs live the third ashtpadi through the three pillars of Sikh life: Naam japna (remembering God), kirat karni (honest work) and vand chhakna (sharing), so that remembrance shows up in action.
